content.overview: Section 4 of the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 empowers the Central Government to appoint officers with such designations as it thinks fit for the purposes of the Act and to entrust them with such powers and functions as it may deem fit. It supports the administrative machinery needed to implement s. 3 measures, standards, inspections and directions.
content.glance: Ask: (1) Was the officer appointed under s. 4? (2) What powers were entrusted? (3) Was the action within that entrustment?
content.study:
s. 4 is an enabling appointment provision. Validity of an officer's act often turns on whether appointment and entrustment cover the function exercised.

No new case invented.

sections.heading: Power to appoint
sections.body: Central Government may appoint officers for the purposes of the Act with designations it thinks fit.

sections.heading: Entrustment of functions
sections.body: Appointed officers may be entrusted with such powers and functions as the Central Government deems fit.

sections.heading: Link to s. 3
sections.body: Appointment machinery supports measures, standards and directions under the Central Government's s. 3 powers.

sections.heading: Challenge points
sections.body: Absence of appointment or entrustment, or action beyond entrusted functions, may be raised in defence of an administrative step.

sections.heading: Method
sections.body: Identify the officer, the instrument of appointment/entrustment and the function exercised.

provisions.title: Appointment of officers and their powers and functions

examples.title: Inspection authority
examples.body: An officer claiming inspection powers under the EPA must show appointment under s. 4 and entrustment of that function.

hypotheticals.question: Can any government officer exercise EPA powers without s. 4 appointment?
hypotheticals.analysis: s. 4 is the appointment gateway for officers for the purposes of the Act; functions must be entrusted as the section contemplates.

distinctions.title: s. 4 appointment vs s. 5 directions
distinctions.right: Empowers Central Government to issue directions in writing to any person, officer or authority.

misconceptions.trap: s. 4 itself creates all environmental duties.
misconceptions.correction: s. 4 is appointment machinery; substantive duties arise under other sections and rules.
